description: How persisted EvalResults roll up into the four product areas of the HAR-145 Ghost Eval Control Plane. An EvalResult's eval_type belongs to exactly one registry family (contracts/evals/eval_registry.json, E1-E22), and each family to exactly one area. HAR-145 puts ACT (artifact, tools, execution) under Decision & Learning, so E13 (tool use, permissions, writes) and E14 (environment / workflow outcome) are there; System is operational only (E18-E22). The operational diagnostics M1-M5 are metrics, never evals, and belong to no area (they are served as OperationalMetrics). family_spans says which TraceSpan kind (episode_trace.v1.json) an EvalResult of a family is attached to; the validation and safety families E18-E22 have no span and are listed on the trace as unassigned. core-go/internal/evalarea mirrors this file; a parity test keeps them identical.

source.section: API / data contracts required from backend (EvalFamilySummary)
source.note: The registry links E-evals to catalog types many-to-many and leaves 13 catalog types unlinked; this file picks the one primary family per type, and a test checks it is one of the registry's own links where the registry has any.
